public_rationale: Microsoft's disclosed investment confirms large company-wide spending, but does not establish the cost of the consumer Copilot push. Google's positive account of Gemini momentum is qualitative. The evidence does not settle sustained January adoption for both products or spending attributable to those consumer efforts. Calling the claim supported would require unsupported allocation and success-threshold assumptions.
limitations: Corporate capital expenditures include activities beyond consumer assistants.
Web traffic share does not measure adoption across all consumer surfaces.
The company's qualitative momentum statement is not independent measurement.
Later growth cannot settle whether the products had already failed when the post appeared.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft and Google have failed to drive consumer adoption of Copilot and Gemini while burning billions.

statement.excerpt: While Microsoft and Google may make money outside of consumer software, both companies have desperately tried to cram Copilot and Gemini down consumers' throats, and they have categorically, unquestionably failed, all while burning billions of dollars to do so.

from_speaker: burning billions of dollars to do so
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that both consumer products failed to achieve meaningful sustained adoption despite billions spent on their consumer pushes.
Enterprise Copilot sales, GitHub Copilot, and general cloud demand do not directly settle this consumer claim.

Use January 2025 for consumer adoption, as specified by the surrounding figures, and October–December 2024 as the latest reported quarter for ongoing spending. The combined target interval covers both.
Read burning billions as spending, consistent with the surrounding capital-expenditure discussion, rather than as a separately quantified net loss.
The surrounding discussion cites company financial figures, so the spending basis is company_reported. Allocation of that spending to consumer adoption remains unproved.
No numerical adoption threshold is added.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence establishes failed sustained consumer uptake for both products and billions in spending attributable to those consumer efforts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes substantial sustained consumer adoption for either product, defeating the assertion that both categorically failed, or complete attributable spending records disprove the billions claim.
